In July 2023, Twitter officially dropped its name and iconic bird logo, rebranding as “X” with the letter X as its symbol. The name carries deep meaning for Musk, who owned the domain X.com back in 1999 before ceding it a couple of years later to PayPal. He finally bought back the domain name in 2017, ultimately bestowing it upon the social media platform.

title: So What Do We Call Twitter Now Anyway?
text:
With a simple name change, Elon Musk has created confusion in social media.

The bewilderment stems from Mr. Musk’s move last month to rebrand Twitter, which he owns, as X. No major social media app has undergone such a name change before, at least while it had tens of millions of active users.

In 2016, Snapchat dropped “chat” from its corporate name, but kept the app’s name unchanged. When Facebook changed its parent company name to Meta in 2021, it also left the name of its flagship social network alone.

The rebranding has been hair-raising for Twitter fans, who embraced the company’s iconic blue-and-white bird logo and used a bird-related lexicon when talking about the platform. A tweet referred to a post; tweeting was a verb for posting, and sharing another person’s post was known as retweeting.

title: Operation Bluebird Launches Twitter.now as Trademark Battle With Elon Musk's X Continues - PhoneWorld
text:
Operation Bluebird has launched a new website, Twitter.now, while its legal trademark battle with Elon Musk’s social media platform X over the former Twitter brand remains unresolved.

The launch follows Operation Bluebird’s efforts to claim trademark rights associated with the original Twitter identity. The organisation argues that X abandoned parts of the former Twitter branding after Musk renamed the platform in 2023.

...

The trademark dispute centres on whether X still holds rights to the Twitter name, the term “tweet” and the platform’s well-known blue bird logo.

...

Operation Bluebird argues that X abandoned parts of the original Twitter identity when it replaced the Twitter name and bird branding with X.

...

The launch does not mean that Operation Bluebird has won the rights to the original Twitter trademarks. The court still needs to resolve the dispute, and no final decision has established who can legally use the contested branding.

# Twitter is officially X.com now

The social network formerly known as Twitter has switched over to X.com.

The social network formerly known as Twitter has switched over to X.com.

by Jay Peters

May 17, 2024, 7:19 AM UTC

The Verge

The social network formerly known as Twitter has officially adopted X.com for all its core systems. That means typing twitter.com in your browser will now redirect to Elon Musk’s favored domain, or should. At the time of publication, we’re seeing a mix of results depending upon browser choice and whether you’re logged in or not.

A message also now appears at the bottom of the X login page that reads, “We are letting you know that we are changing our URL, but your privacy and data protection settings remain the same.”

The domain transition has been one of the more awkward aspects of Elon Musk’s move to rebrand the company. Although many aspects of X migrated to the new branding long ago — including its official account, its mobile apps, and its “X Premium” (fka Blue) subscriptions — the platform’s URLs have remained twitter.com ever since Musk officially initiated the switch to X.

...

Maybe, but one thing’s for sure: it’s not Twitter anymore.
